title: Computer Science Foundations — Order in God's Digital Creation: Unit Quiz

questions.question: Who is often called the 'father of the computer' for designing the Analytical Engine?
options: Blaise Pascal
Charles Babbage
Alan Turing
Claude Shannon
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine in 1837, which contained the fundamental concepts of modern computing: input, processing, memory, and output.

questions.question: Why do computers use the binary (base-2) number system?
options: Because binary is easier for humans to understand
Because electronic components naturally represent two states: on and off
Because binary was invented before the decimal system
Because binary uses less electricity than other number systems
questions.explanation: Electronic components can easily represent two states — on/off, high/low voltage — which correspond to the binary digits 1 and 0. This makes binary the natural language of electronic computers.

questions.question: How many different values can a single byte (8 bits) represent?
questions.explanation: A byte contains 8 bits, and each bit can be 0 or 1. The total number of combinations is 2^8 = 256 different values.

questions.question: What advantage does a binary search have over a linear search?
options: It works on unsorted data
It is dramatically faster for large, sorted datasets
It uses less memory
It can search multiple items at once
questions.explanation: A binary search repeatedly divides the search area in half, making it dramatically faster than a linear search for large sorted datasets. It can find an item among a million sorted items in at most 20 steps.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a compiler?
options: To find and fix bugs in a program
To translate high-level programming language into machine code
To connect a computer to the internet
To store data in the computer's memory
questions.explanation: A compiler translates an entire program written in a high-level programming language into machine code (binary) that the computer can execute directly.

questions.question: Who developed the first compiler, making programming more accessible to non-specialists?
options: Ada Lovelace
Alan Turing
Grace Hopper
Tim Berners-Lee
questions.explanation: Grace Hopper, a pioneering computer scientist and devout Christian, led the development of the first compiler (A-0) in 1952. She believed computers should be accessible to as many people as possible.

questions.question: What is the first phase of the Software Development Lifecycle?
options: Writing code
Testing the software
Planning and requirements analysis
Deploying the software
questions.explanation: The SDLC begins with planning and requirements analysis — understanding what the software needs to do before any code is written. Skipping this phase leads to building software that does not solve the right problem.

questions.question: According to Frederick Brooks in The Mythical Man-Month, what happens when you add more people to a late software project?
options: The project finishes faster
The project becomes later due to increased communication overhead
The project cost decreases
The quality of the software improves
questions.explanation: Brooks observed that adding people to a late project makes it even later because new team members need time to get up to speed and the increased number of communication channels adds complexity.

questions.question: What does Claude Shannon's information theory establish?
options: That computers will eventually become conscious
That all information can be measured and represented using binary digits
That the internet should be free for everyone
That programming languages should use English words
questions.explanation: Shannon's information theory established that all information, regardless of its form, can be measured mathematically and represented using binary digits (bits). This foundational insight made modern digital communication possible.

questions.question: C.S. Lewis warned in The Abolition of Man that technology without moral truth becomes dangerous because:
options: Technology always breaks down eventually
Only scientists understand technology well enough to use it
It becomes a tool for those in power to reshape the world without moral limits
Technology is inherently evil and should be avoided
questions.explanation: Lewis argued that without objective moral truth grounded in God's created order, technological power has no moral boundaries and becomes a tool for whoever holds it to impose their will on others without accountability to a higher standard.
